reason_summary: Low, at the floor of the band. Shanan's risk-of-bias row was verified directly against the assessment file: SERIOUS overall on SERIOUS confounding, with MODERATE selection or sorting, MODERATE treatment classification, LOW outcome measurement, LOW missing data, MODERATE selective reporting. The SERIOUS rating did not move me off Low. PROTOCOL 4.1 places 'one credible quasi-experiment without replication' at Low and reserves Very low for evidence that is correlational only, mechanism speculative, or inconsistent in pattern, and none of the three describes Shanan: the design carries state and cohort variation, neighboring-border comparisons, placebo exposure, alternative staggered-treatment estimators and mortality checks; the first link of the chain is measured rather than assumed, with child employment down 0.029 (SE 0.008) on a 0.118 base and attendance up 0.042 (SE 0.008); and with one on-target estimate in the corpus there is no second result for the pattern to be inconsistent with. SERIOUS is also not CRITICAL, and CRITICAL is the level at which a design stops supplying usable evidence. What the SERIOUS rating does change is where inside Low this sits, and it belongs at the bottom, because the named confounder is not boilerplate. Adoption endogeneity is precisely the rival account Greenwood and Seshadri (2004) set out, in which rising demand for skill pulled children out of work and fertility fell first, with legislatures codifying afterward. That account reproduces Shanan's correlation with no causal role for the law, and nothing in the record rules it out. Two further gaps compound it: the middle link, the fall in what a child was worth to its parents, is inferred from its two ends and never measured in dollars, and the child-quality channel is observationally equivalent inside the same coefficient, so even a fully credible -0.301 would not be attributed to this hypothesis rather than to the quantity-quality account next door. Demographic significance is partial. The 8% share reproduces exactly (0.48 * 0.85 / 5 = 0.0816), and the analytic interval of 6.1% to 10.2% reproduces from the reported SE of 0.11, but the figure sits below the protocol's 10% bar, is computed on an annual birth probability at a single age in a single country rather than on the completed fertility this hypothesis names, holds two of its three inputs fixed for want of a bootstrap, covers three decades of one national episode rather than the FDT, and inherits the SERIOUS confounding, which under the adoption-endogeneity story is signed toward overstatement, so 8% reads better as a ceiling than as a center. Partial rather than not significant because the number is real, reproducible and non-trivial; partial rather than significant because no route in 4.2 clears a threshold. Escalate to the PI on two questions a rater cannot settle from the protocol as written. First, whether 'credible' in the Low cell carries an implicit risk-of-bias condition. Textbook GRADE starts observational evidence at Low and downgrades a level for serious risk of bias, which would land this at Very low; this review's adapted table prices the non-randomized design into the Low cell itself and so does not downgrade twice. I applied the project's table, which is the governing document, but the divergence will recur in every chapter and should be settled once rather than per rater. Second, whether a sub-threshold 8% whose upper bound crosses 10% maps to partial or to not significant, since 4.2 states a binary rule and 4.3 offers a four-way menu with no mapping between them; the chapter's own note to co-authors already flags that the two texts disagree.

Shanan (2023) is the sole on-target study, and its SERIOUS overall / SERIOUS confounding rating was verified and weighed but does not push the rating below Low. ROBINS-I SERIOUS is not CRITICAL: the assessment itself credits state/cohort and neighboring-border designs, placebo exposure, alternative staggered-treatment estimators, and mortality checks, and PROTOCOL 4.1's Low band already admits strictly weaker evidence ('cross-sectional or panel with controls, no clear identification'), so a design of this quality cannot sit beneath it. Very low requires correlational-only evidence, a speculative mechanism, or an inconsistent pattern, and none of the three holds: the first link of the chain is directly measured (child employment -0.029 on a 0.118 baseline; attendance +0.042 on 0.882), and the completed-fertility (-0.301, SE 0.044) and annual-birth-probability (-0.0085, SE 0.0011) estimates agree in direction and both survive joint entry of the two policy margins. Downgrading further for adoption endogeneity would double-count the defect that already caps the rating at Low through non-replication, since the risk-of-bias rationale and the no-second-setting ceiling name the same limitation. The unresolved competition between lost child earnings and the child-quality channel is the strongest argument for Very low and is what keeps this at the floor of Low rather than comfortably inside it. Demographic significance is partial: the 8% share is below 4.2's 10% bar and the slope-sufficiency and conditional R-squared routes met no threshold, but the analytic interval reaches 10.2% and is understated by construction because two of three inputs are held fixed, and the share is computed on an annual birth probability at a single age rather than on the completed-fertility quantum the hypothesis names. PI escalation is warranted on two grounds no rater can settle: 4.1 supplies no rule for adjusting a GRADE level for a study-level risk-of-bias rating, a protocol gap that will recur in every chapter of the review, and the significance verdict straddles a 10% threshold that 4.2 states as binary while 4.3 offers a 'partial' level the protocol never defines.

Low rather than very_low. Shanan (2023) is a single unreplicated quasi-experiment, which is verbatim the protocol's own definition of Low, and the SERIOUS confounding rating does not push it out the bottom of that tier because the tier's stated floor already admits panel designs with no clear identification at all. Very low is reserved for evidence that is correlational only, speculative in mechanism, or inconsistent in pattern; a 1.37m-child, 336k-woman staggered state/cohort design with neighboring-border pairs, placebo exposure, alternative staggered-treatment estimators, mortality checks, and a measured first stage on the correct generation (child employment -0.029 SE 0.008, attendance +0.042 SE 0.008) is none of the three, and with one estimate there is no pattern that can be inconsistent. ROBINS-I SERIOUS is also not CRITICAL: the framework reserves CRITICAL for studies too problematic to enter a synthesis, so a SERIOUS study remains usable evidence, weakened. The SERIOUS rating did not change the label but it consumes any headroom inside it, for two reasons the original panel could not weigh. First, the confounder is not generic: Greenwood and Seshadri (2004), a theory paper in this same corpus, argue that skill-biased technological progress drove both the withdrawal of children from work and the fertility decline, with effective regulation arriving after the movement had begun, which is precisely the adoption endogeneity the SERIOUS rating names. Second, the hypothesis's middle link, the fall in what a child was worth to its parents, is never measured and is inferred from the two links on either side of it, while policy bundling and the child-quality channel supply a rival account predicting the same first and third links; the joint specification (any restriction -0.0050 SE 0.0013, exit age -0.0018 SE 0.0004) comes closest to separating them and does not separate them. Theory gives no prior to lean on either, since Baland and Robinson (2000) prove the sign ambiguous and Takakura (2023) gets opposite signs across household types. I did not weigh the six own-schooling studies or their nulls, which test arrow (2) and belong to the tempo chapter. Demographic significance partial, on a share of 8% computed as 0.48 * 0.85 / 5: below the protocol's 10% bar, measured on an annual birth probability at a single age rather than the TFR change 4.2 names, from one country, with no bootstrap CI as 4.2 requires. Escalate to the PI on three grounds that are protocol readings rather than evidence weighings: whether the Low tier absorbs a SERIOUS ROBINS-I rating or whether standard GRADE downgrading should apply on top of a table that already prices design into the tier; whether an unmeasured middle link with a live observationally equivalent rival counts as 'mechanism speculative' under the very_low row; and whether a point estimate below the 10% threshold whose only interval, 6.1% to 10.2%, crosses it and is itself understated by holding two of three inputs fixed reads as partial or as not significant, a threshold-policy call the chapter's own note to co-authors already flags as unresolved.
